title: Huaynaputina eruption of 1600
summary: A large Plinian eruption began on 19 February 1600 at Huaynaputina, a stratovolcano in southern Peru, and continued into about early March. Rated VEI 6, it is the largest historical eruption in the Andes; Lavallée and colleagues estimate over 11 km3 of magma in three stages. A 2022 study links it to exceptional cooling in 1601 but calls the evidence consistent with, not proof of, a lasting climate trigger.

uncertainty.note: Start date from White et al. (2022); activity continued into about early March.

as_recorded.value: A large Plinian eruption took place on February 19
